reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and independently developed IP with only a limited processing right to Vendor and no transfer of rights.

14.2 gives Customer ownership of each Deliverable with a present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurance cooperation, matching the preferred position (Vendor assigns work product).

14.3 permits Vendor to retain Vendor Technology (expressly acceptable under the rule) but channels embedded Vendor Technology into the 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works for Customer's business, satisfying the licence-back requirement.

14.4 bars joint ownership absent a signed instrument fixing exploitation rights and keeps Feedback voluntary with Customer retaining unrestricted use of its own feedback, so no walk-away trigger is present.
Definitions are consistent (Vendor Technology expressly excludes Customer Data and pre-existing Customer IP; Customer Data captures derived output), so no definitional back-door assignment exists.

Redline is unchanged and no counterparty comment was proposed, which is the correct output for a compliant finding; the deterministic check confirming no residual assignment of Customer IP/Data to Vendor also passes.
